tools.name: check_domain
tools.description: Use this when someone asks whether a domain's email authentication is set up correctly, why mail from a domain fails DMARC, SPF or DKIM, or which DNS records to publish for it. Reads the domain's live DMARC, SPF and DKIM records and returns what is wrong with each, plus the records to add or change.

tools.name: build_spf
tools.description: Use this when someone lists the services that send their email and wants the SPF record to publish, or wants a sender added to the SPF record they already have. Takes provider names such as Google Workspace or Mailchimp, include terms such as include:spf.example.com, or IP addresses, and returns one

tools.name: explain_bounce
tools.description: Use this when someone pastes a bounce message, an SMTP reply such as 550 5.7.26, or an Authentication-Results header and asks what it means or how to fix it. Returns what the receiving server refused, what to change, when it clears, and the page that explains it. Works from the pasted text alone and

tools.name: analyze_report
tools.description: Use this when someone has a DMARC aggregate report and wants to know which senders passed and which failed. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_domain, analyze_report · Private data: check_domain, build_spf, explain_bounce, analyze_report · Public sink: check_domain, build_spf, analyze_report.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_domain, analyze_report · Private data: check_domain, build_spf, explain_bounce, analyze_report · Public sink: check_domain, build_spf, analyze_report

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
